_comment: The Sources shelf: every work the app draws on or cites, one card each, so anyone can see what a source is, who made it, when, its license, and where to read or find it. atlas build reads this file (crates/atlas-cli/src/shelf.rs) with sources.json and the sources config/aramaic.json cites, and writes shelf.json for the Sources tab.
groups: the shelves, in the order shown. id: lowercase letters and hyphens, named by a work's group. name: the plain heading.

works: one card per work. id: unique, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; a work that is a dataset uses its sources.json id. group: a groups id. plain: what the Simple level shows, the kind of work and when, in words anyone understands (48 characters at most), such as "Bible dictionary, 1897", or for a book or article what it is about, such as "Article on the word Abba, 1988". title. by: who wrote or made it. when: as shown, such as "1897" or "around AD 200". what: one or two plain, modest sentences (240 characters at most).

license: public-domain, cc-by-4.0, cc-by-sa-4.0 or copyrighted; licenseNote (optional) says more, such as a dataset's license beside its text's. The app ships only public domain, CC BY 4.0 and CC BY-SA 4.0 material. A copyrighted work is cited and linked, never quoted at length or stored.

datasets: the sources.json ids whose pinned files are this work; [] for a work the app only cites. Each sources.json id belongs to exactly one work. A dataset no work claims still gets a plain card made from sources.json, with a build warning.

read: where to read the whole work free, either {"app": "bible"} or {"app": "dictionary"} inside the app, or {"url", "label"} for a free full copy of that very work, checked by opening it. Never for a copyrighted work. find: {"url", "label"}, a link for the citation: https://doi.org/ and the DOI when there is one, else a publisher or library catalog page, else a WorldCat search. Required for a copyrighted work. Links are https only.

citation: the full bibliographic citation, shown at Deep. cites: parts of the source strings the app shows (config/aramaic.json sources) that name this work. The build records where the app cites each work and warns about any source string no work matches. Keep each one long enough to match only this work's strings; plain ASCII is safest.

To add a work: add one entry with facts checked against the work itself, its publisher or a library catalog, never guessed; give it cites for each source string that names it; if it is a dataset, pin it in sources.json and credit it in NOTICE.md as well. Works only drafted in config/layers.json are added when they go live.

works.title: Berean Standard Bible (BSB)
works.by: The Berean Bible Translation Committee, with Bible Hub, Discovery Bible and OpenBible.com
works.what: A modern English translation from the Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek. It is the English you read in this app, with its own footnotes and section headings.
works.licenseNote: Dedicated to the public domain on 30 April 2023.
works.citation: The Holy Bible, Berean Standard Bible (BSB), produced in cooperation with Bible Hub, Discovery Bible, OpenBible.com and the Berean Bible Translation Committee (2016; dedicated to the public domain 30 April 2023), https://berean.bible/. Text via scrollmapper/bible_databases; footnotes and section headings via the USFM edition in usfm-bible/examples.bsb.

works.title: King James Version (KJV)
works.by: Translators appointed under King James I; the 1769 Oxford text edited by Benjamin Blayney
works.what: The best-known older English Bible. The app never shows it: search uses its wording so a verse remembered in King James words is still found.
works.licenseNote: Public domain in most of the world; in the United Kingdom the Crown's rights in the KJV are managed by Cambridge University Press.
works.citation: The Holy Bible, King James Version (1611), Oxford standard text of 1769 (ed. Benjamin Blayney). Text via scrollmapper/bible_databases (public domain).

works.title: American Standard Version (ASV)
works.by: The American committee of the English Revised Version
works.what: An American revision of the King James Bible. The app never shows it: search uses its wording so a verse remembered in words close to the ASV is still found.
works.citation: The Holy Bible, American Standard Version (New York: Thomas Nelson & Sons, 1901). Text via scrollmapper/bible_databases (public domain).

works.plain: Hebrew Old Testament, word by word
works.title: Translators Amalgamated Hebrew OT (TAHOT)
works.by: STEPBible.org, based on work at Tyndale House, Cambridge
works.what: Every Hebrew and Aramaic word of the Old Testament, from the Leningrad Codex, with its root, its grammar and an English meaning.
works.citation: STEPBible, TAHOT: Translators Amalgamated Hebrew OT. Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0). github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data. This copy: October 2026.

works.plain: Greek New Testament, word by word
works.title: Translators Amalgamated Greek NT (TAGNT)
works.by: STEPBible.org, based on work at Tyndale House, Cambridge
works.what: Every Greek word of the New Testament in the major printed editions, with its root, its grammar, an English meaning and which editions have it.
works.citation: STEPBible, TAGNT: Translators Amalgamated Greek NT (NA27/28, SBL, Tyndale House, Westcott-Hort, Tregelles, Textus Receptus and Byzantine editions). Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0). github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data. This copy: October 2026.

works.title: The Peshitta New Testament (Digital Syriac Corpus)
works.by: Digital Syriac Corpus: edition by James E. Walters, Syriac text typed by George A. Kiraz
works.what: The New Testament in Syriac, a dialect of Aramaic, translated from the Greek. The app shows it at Deep beside the English, as a translation and never as Jesus' own words.
works.licenseNote: The digital edition is CC BY 4.0; the Syriac text, printed in 1905, is public domain.

read.label: Digital Syriac Corpus, starting at Matthew

works.citation: The New Testament in Syriac (British and Foreign Bible Society, 1905). Digital Syriac Corpus (syriaccorpus.org): TEI XML edition by James E. Walters, Syriac text transcribed by George A. Kiraz, CC BY 4.0.

works.plain: Word links from Hebrew and Greek to English
works.title: Clear Bible word alignments for the BSB
works.by: Clear Bible (Biblica); the Greek links made by the Berean Bible team, the Hebrew by BiblioNexus
works.what: Links from each Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek word to the words of the BSB that translate it, made by hand. They let the app color matching words.
works.licenseNote: The alignments are CC BY 4.0; the Hebrew (WLC) and BSB texts they link are public domain.
works.citation: Clear Bible / Biblica, Alignments: BSB manual alignments WLCM-BSB and BGNT-BSB, github.com/Clear-Bible/Alignments (CC BY 4.0). This copy: May 2026.

works.plain: Hebrew words with their Greek match
works.title: MACULA Hebrew Linguistic Datasets
works.what: Word-by-word data on the Hebrew Old Testament. The app uses one part: for each Hebrew word, the Greek word the Septuagint (the ancient Greek Old Testament) uses there.
works.licenseNote: The data is CC BY 4.0 (Biblica); the Hebrew text it annotates, the Westminster Leningrad Codex, is public domain.
works.citation: MACULA Hebrew Linguistic Datasets, (C) Biblica, Inc., CC BY 4.0, github.com/Clear-Bible/macula-hebrew.

works.title: OpenBible.info Cross References
works.what: About 340,000 pairs of related verses, built mostly from the Treasury of Scripture Knowledge, with readers' votes on how closely each pair is related.
works.citation: OpenBible.info, Cross References (file dated 2024-11-04), https://www.openbible.info/labs/cross-references/ (CC BY 4.0), via the unmodified copy in scrollmapper/bible_databases.

works.title: Easton's Bible Dictionary
works.what: A Scottish minister's dictionary of the people, places and things of the Bible, first called the Illustrated Bible Dictionary. Written in the 1800s, so some of what it says is out of date.
works.licenseNote: The dictionary is public domain. This copy is the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's transcription, carried by CCEL Paragraphs (CC BY-SA 4.0) and NEUU's Bible Dictionary Dataset (CC BY 4.0).
works.citation: M. G. Easton, Illustrated Bible Dictionary, 3rd ed. (Thomas Nelson, 1897), known as Easton's Bible Dictionary. Text from the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's transcription, via CCEL Paragraphs by Jon Craton (CC BY-SA 4.0) and the Bible Dictionary Dataset, Copyright (c) 2026 NEUU, github.com/neuu-org/bible-dictionary-dataset (CC BY 4.0).

works.title: Smith's Bible Dictionary
works.by: William Smith; this edition revised by F. N. and M. A. Peloubet
works.what: A one-volume American edition of William Smith's Dictionary of the Bible, with notes added by its editors. Written in the 1800s, so some of what it says is out of date.
works.licenseNote: The dictionary is public domain. This copy is the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's transcription, carried by CCEL Paragraphs (CC BY-SA 4.0) and NEUU's Bible Dictionary Dataset (CC BY 4.0).
works.citation: William Smith, Smith's Bible Dictionary, the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's edition, dated 1884: the American edition revised and edited by F. N. and M. A. Peloubet (Philadelphia: Porter & Coates, 1884). First published as A Dictionary of the Bible (London: John Murray, 1860–1863). Text from the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's transcription, via CCEL Paragraphs by Jon Craton (CC BY-SA 4.0) and the Bible Dictionary Dataset, Copyright (c) 2026 NEUU, github.com/neuu-org/bible-dictionary-dataset (CC BY 4.0).

works.title: Nave's Topical Bible
works.what: More than 20,000 subjects, each with the verses that speak of it. Ask the Bible uses it only as an index to gather verses; none of Nave's own words are shown.
works.licenseNote: The table edition the app reads is CC BY 4.0 (Brady Stephenson, BibleData); Nave's book itself is public domain.
works.citation: Orville J. Nave, Nave's Topical Bible (Lincoln, Nebraska: Topical Bible Publishing Co., 1896–1897). Table edition: Brady Stephenson, BibleData, github.com/BradyStephenson/bible-data (CC BY 4.0).

works.title: Aquifer Open Study Notes
works.by: Bible scholars at Tyndale House Publishers; plain-English adaptation by Mission Mutual
works.what: Short notes on almost every passage of the Bible, explaining people, places, words and background. They show one tap away from a verse, as these scholars' notes.
works.licenseNote: Aquifer Open Study Notes (C) 2026 Mission Mutual, an adaptation of Tyndale Open Study Notes (C) 2023 Tyndale House Publishers, both CC BY-SA 4.0.
works.citation: Aquifer Open Study Notes, (C) 2026 Mission Mutual, CC BY-SA 4.0, github.com/BibleAquifer/AquiferOpenStudyNotes; adapted from Tyndale Open Study Notes, (C) 2023 Tyndale House Publishers, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://tyndaleopenresources.com.

works.title: Tyndale Open Bible Dictionary
works.by: Tyndale House Publishers; edited by Philip W. Comfort and Walter A. Elwell
works.what: A modern Bible dictionary that Tyndale shares under an open license. The app quotes its articles word for word for when each part of the Bible happened and when each book was written.
works.citation: Tyndale Open Bible Dictionary, ed. Philip W. Comfort and Walter A. Elwell. Copyright (C) 2023 by Tyndale House Publishers. Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. Available free at http://www.tyndaleopenresources.com.

works.title: UBS Fauna, Flora and Realia handbooks
works.by: United Bible Societies; written by Edward R. Hope, Robert Koops and Ray Pritz
works.what: Three handbooks for Bible translators on the animals, plants and human-made things of the Bible. The app shows short articles from them in the word study.
works.citation: Animals in the Bible © United Bible Societies, 2025, adapted from Edward R. Hope, All Creatures Great and Small: Living Things in the Bible © 2005 United Bible Societies; Plants and Trees in the Bible © United Bible Societies, 2025, adapted from Robert Koops, Each According to its Kind: Plants and Trees in the Bible © 2012 United Bible Societies; Human-made Things in the Bible © United Bible Societies, 2025, adapted from Ray Pritz, The Works of Their Hands: Man-made Things in the Bible © 2009 United Bible Societies. CC BY-SA 4.0, github.com/ubsicap/ubs-open-license.

works.plain: Hebrew word list, from a 1906 dictionary
works.title: Translators Brief lexicon of Extended Strongs for Hebrew (TBESH)
works.by: STEPBible.org, based on work at Tyndale House, Cambridge
works.what: Short definitions for every Hebrew and Aramaic word root of the Old Testament, abridged from the Brown-Driver-Briggs lexicon of 1906.
works.citation: STEPBible, TBESH: Translators Brief lexicon of Extended Strongs for Hebrew, based on the Abridged BDB (Online Bible). Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0). github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data. This copy: October 2026.

works.plain: Greek word list, from a 1922 dictionary
works.title: Translators Brief lexicon of Extended Strongs for Greek (TBESG)
works.by: STEPBible.org, based on work at Tyndale House, Cambridge
works.what: Short definitions for every Greek word root of the New Testament, mostly from Abbott-Smith's lexicon of 1922.
works.citation: STEPBible, TBESG: Translators Brief lexicon of Extended Strongs for Greek, based on the definitions of G. Abbott-Smith. Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0). github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data. This copy: October 2026.

works.title: Liddell-Scott-Jones Greek-English Lexicon (STEPBible TFLSJ)
works.by: Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Henry Stuart Jones and Roderick McKenzie; put online by the Perseus Digital Library; formatted and dated by STEPBible
works.what: The great dictionary of ancient Greek, from Homer on. The app uses only its short meanings and the century of the earliest writer it cites for each.
works.licenseNote: The LSJ text from the Perseus Digital Library is CC BY-SA 4.0; STEPBible's formatting and dates are CC BY 4.0.
works.citation: H. G. Liddell, R. Scott, H. S. Jones and R. McKenzie, A Greek-English Lexicon, 9th ed. (Oxford University Press, 1940), from the Perseus Digital Library, Tufts University (CC BY-SA 4.0); formatted, with dates added to authors, as STEPBible TFLSJ: Translators Formatted full LSJ Bible lexicon. Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0). github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data.

works.title: A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament
works.by: Joseph Henry Thayer, from the Latin lexicon of C. L. W. Grimm and C. G. Wilke
works.what: A classic dictionary of New Testament Greek, translated and enlarged by an American scholar. Old, but still widely used.
works.citation: Joseph Henry Thayer, A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament, being Grimm's Wilke's Clavis Novi Testamenti, translated, revised and enlarged (New York: American Book Company, 1889).

works.title: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
works.what: A compact dictionary of New Testament Greek that also notes how the Greek Old Testament uses many of its words. STEPBible's short Greek definitions come mostly from it.
works.citation: G. Abbott-Smith, A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament (Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark, 1922).
cites: G. Abbott-Smith, A Manual Greek Lexicon

works.title: OpenBible.info Bible Geocoding Data
works.what: Every place the Bible names that can be located, the modern sites proposed for it and how sure each one is, with the sources behind them, and the shapes of regions such as Galilee and Edom.
works.licenseNote: Coordinates the dataset takes from OpenStreetMap or Google are left out of the app.
works.citation: OpenBible.info, Bible Geocoding Data (2021), https://www.openbible.info/geo/, github.com/openbibleinfo/Bible-Geocoding-Data (CC BY 4.0).

works.plain: Data on Bible people and places
works.title: Theographic Bible Metadata
works.what: Linked lists of the people, places and events of the Bible. The app uses it to name who was born, died or was present at each place.
works.licenseNote: The people file the app builds from it is shared under the same license.
works.citation: Robert Rouse, Theographic Bible Metadata (viz.bible), github.com/robertrouse/theographic-bible-metadata (CC BY-SA 4.0). This copy: April 2026.

works.title: Natural Earth
works.by: Natural Earth: Tom Patterson, Nathaniel Vaughn Kelso and others
works.what: Free map data of the whole world. The app uses its coastlines, lakes, rivers, sea names and today's borders for the Places map.
works.citation: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com. Version 5.2.0-pre, via github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector.

works.title: The Mishnah
works.by: Rabbi Judah the Prince, from the teachings of earlier rabbis
works.what: The first great written collection of Jewish law and teaching, mostly in Hebrew. The app cites it for words that also appear in the Gospels.
works.licenseNote: The Hebrew text is public domain; Sefaria's English translations carry their own licenses.
works.citation: The Mishnah, compiled by Rabbi Judah ha-Nasi, late 2nd or early 3rd century AD. Cited by tractate, chapter and paragraph (Avot, Taanit).

works.plain: Book defending the Jews, after AD 94
works.title: Against Apion
works.what: A Jewish historian's answer, in Greek, to attacks on the Jewish people. It quotes older Greek writers who mention the Jews and their customs.
works.licenseNote: William Whiston's English translation (1737) is public domain.
works.citation: Flavius Josephus, Against Apion (Greek, after AD 94), cited by book and section; English translation by William Whiston.

works.title: Jewish Antiquities
works.what: A history of the Jewish people in twenty books, written in Greek, from the creation to the war with Rome that began in AD 66.
works.licenseNote: William Whiston's English translation (1737) is public domain.
works.citation: Flavius Josephus, Jewish Antiquities (Greek, AD 94), cited by book and section; English translation by William Whiston.

works.plain: Jewish commentary on Genesis, 1st century AD
works.title: Allegorical Interpretation
works.what: A Jewish thinker's commentary, in Greek, on passages of Genesis, read as pictures of the soul. It explains names such as Melchizedek and Salem.
works.licenseNote: C. D. Yonge's English translation (1854–55) is public domain.
works.citation: Philo of Alexandria, Allegorical Interpretation (Legum allegoriae), cited by book and section. English translation: "On the Allegories of the Sacred Laws", in The Works of Philo Judaeus, translated by C. D. Yonge, vol. 1 (London: Bohn, 1854).

works.title: The Didache (The Teaching of the Twelve Apostles)
works.when: 1st century AD, as most scholars date it
works.what: A short early Christian guide to how to live, baptize and share the Lord's Supper, written in Greek. One of its prayers keeps the Aramaic word Maranatha.
works.citation: The Didache, or Teaching of the Twelve Apostles (Greek, 1st century AD), cited by chapter and verse. Known from a Greek manuscript of 1056 published by Philotheos Bryennios in 1883. English translation in J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers.

works.title: 4 Ezra (2 Esdras 3–14)
works.by: An unknown Jewish writer, in Ezra's name
works.what: Visions written in Ezra's name after Jerusalem fell in AD 70, kept in Latin and other translations. Some Bibles print it among the Apocrypha as 2 Esdras.
works.licenseNote: G. H. Box's English translation (1917) is public domain in the United States.
works.citation: 4 Ezra (2 Esdras 3–14), late 1st century AD. English translation: G. H. Box, The Apocalypse of Ezra (II Esdras iii–xiv), Translated from the Syriac (London: SPCK, 1917). Verses 7:36–105, missing from most Latin copies, were published by R. L. Bensly in 1875.

works.title: Targum of Psalms
works.when: date unknown; the oldest dated copy is from 1237–1238
works.what: An Aramaic rendering of the Psalms made for Jewish readers. At Psalm 22 its words are close to Jesus' cry from the cross.
works.citation: Targum of Psalms (Aramaic), text of the Mikraot Gedolot as given by Sefaria (public domain). Its date is uncertain; the oldest dated manuscript is the Breslau manuscript of 1237–1238.

works.plain: Edition of a Dead Sea Scroll, 1962
works.title: The Copper Scroll (3Q15), in Discoveries in the Judaean Desert III
works.by: Unknown; edited by J. T. Milik, with R. de Vaux and H. W. Baker
works.what: A list of hidden treasure engraved on copper, found in a cave near Qumran in 1952. The app cites it for a place name often linked with the pool of Bethesda.
works.licenseNote: The scroll is ancient; the 1962 edition that publishes it is under copyright.
works.citation: J. T. Milik, "Le rouleau de cuivre provenant de la grotte 3Q (3Q15)", with R. de Vaux and H. W. Baker, in M. Baillet, J. T. Milik and R. de Vaux, Les 'Petites Grottes' de Qumrân, Discoveries in the Judaean Desert of Jordan III (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1962), 201–302.

works.title: A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament
works.what: Explains, passage by passage, why the editors of the standard Greek New Testament chose one wording where old copies differ.
works.citation: Bruce M. Metzger, A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament, 2nd ed. (Stuttgart: Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft / German Bible Society, 1994).
cites: Bruce M. Metzger, A Textual Commentary

works.plain: Article on the languages of Jesus' land, 1970
works.title: The Languages of Palestine in the First Century A.D.
works.what: A survey of the languages used in the land of Israel in Jesus' time: Latin, Greek, Aramaic and Hebrew.
works.citation: Joseph A. Fitzmyer, "The Languages of Palestine in the First Century A.D.", Catholic Biblical Quarterly 32 (1970): 501–531.
cites: The Languages of Palestine in the First Century

works.title: Aramaic Kephaʾ and Peter's Name in the New Testament
works.what: A study of the Aramaic word kepha, rock, and of how it became Peter's name, Cephas.
works.citation: Joseph A. Fitzmyer, "Aramaic Kephaʾ and Peter's Name in the New Testament", in Ernest Best and R. McL. Wilson (eds.), Text and Interpretation: Studies in the New Testament Presented to Matthew Black (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1979), 121–132.

works.title: New Testament Kyrios and Maranatha and Their Aramaic Background
works.what: Argues from the Aramaic prayer Maranatha that Jesus was called Lord in Aramaic very early.
works.citation: Joseph A. Fitzmyer, "New Testament Kyrios and Maranatha and Their Aramaic Background", in To Advance the Gospel: New Testament Studies, 2nd ed., The Biblical Resource Series (Grand Rapids: Eerdmans, 1998), 218–235.

works.title: The Aramaic Qorbān Inscription from Jebel Ḫallet eṭ-Ṭûri and Mk 7:11/Mt 15:5
works.what: On an Aramaic inscription from near Jerusalem that uses the word qorban, offering, in the sense Jesus quotes in Mark 7:11.
works.citation: Joseph A. Fitzmyer, "The Aramaic Qorbān Inscription from Jebel Ḫallet eṭ-Ṭûri and Mk 7:11/Mt 15:5", Journal of Biblical Literature 78 (1959): 60–65; reprinted in The Semitic Background of the New Testament (Grand Rapids: Eerdmans, 1997), 93–100.

works.title: ʾAbbā Isn't 'Daddy'
works.what: Argues that Abba, the Aramaic word Jesus used for God, means father, and not a child's word like Daddy.
works.citation: James Barr, "ʾAbbā Isn't 'Daddy'", Journal of Theological Studies 39.1 (1988): 28–47, https://doi.org/10.1093/jts/39.1.28.

works.title: ΒΑΡΝΑΒΑΣ: ϒΙΟΣ ΠΑΡΑΚΛΗΣΕΩΣ
works.what: On the name Barnabas, and why Acts 4:36 explains it as Son of Encouragement.
works.citation: Sebastian Brock, "ΒΑΡΝΑΒΑΣ: ϒΙΟΣ ΠΑΡΑΚΛΗΣΕΩΣ", Journal of Theological Studies n.s. 25.1 (1974): 93–98, https://doi.org/10.1093/jts/XXV.1.93.

works.plain: Article on the words for Hebrew, 2019
works.title: Ancient Names for Hebrew and Aramaic: A Case for Lexical Revision
works.what: Argues that the Greek word for "in Hebrew" means Hebrew, not Aramaic, and that dictionaries should say so.
works.citation: Ken M. Penner, "Ancient Names for Hebrew and Aramaic: A Case for Lexical Revision", New Testament Studies 65.3 (2019): 412–423, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0028688519000067.

works.plain: Chapter on the words for Hebrew, 2014
works.title: Hebraisti in Ancient Texts: Does Ἑβραϊστί Ever Mean 'Aramaic'?
works.what: Looks at how ancient texts use the Greek word for "in Hebrew" and asks whether it ever means Aramaic.
works.citation: Randall Buth and Chad Pierce, "Hebraisti in Ancient Texts: Does Ἑβραϊστί Ever Mean 'Aramaic'?", in Randall Buth and R. Steven Notley (eds.), The Language Environment of First Century Judaea, Jerusalem Studies in the Synoptic Gospels 2 (Leiden: Brill, 2014), chapter 3.

works.plain: Chapter on Jesus' cry from the cross, 2014
works.title: The Riddle of Jesus' Cry from the Cross
works.what: Asks why Matthew and Mark give Jesus' cry from the cross in different forms, Eli and Eloi, and what each one tells the reader.
works.citation: Randall Buth, "The Riddle of Jesus' Cry from the Cross: The Meaning of ηλι ηλι λαμα σαβαχθανι (Matthew 27:46) and the Literary Function of ελωι ελωι λειμα σαβαχθανι (Mark 15:34)", in Randall Buth and R. Steven Notley (eds.), The Language Environment of First Century Judaea, Jerusalem Studies in the Synoptic Gospels 2 (Leiden: Brill, 2014), chapter 11.

works.title: The Death of the Messiah, volume 2
works.what: A detailed commentary on the Gospel accounts of Jesus' arrest, trials, death and burial. Volume 2 includes his cry from the cross.
works.citation: Raymond E. Brown, The Death of the Messiah: From Gethsemane to the Grave, vol. 2, Anchor Bible Reference Library (New York: Doubleday, 1994).
cites: Raymond E. Brown, The Death of the Messiah

works.title: Ἐφφαθά (Mark VII.34): Certainly Hebrew, not Aramaic
works.what: Argues that Ephphatha, Jesus' word to a deaf man in Mark 7:34, is Hebrew rather than Aramaic.
works.citation: Isaac Rabinowitz, "Ἐφφαθά (Mark VII.34): Certainly Hebrew, not Aramaic", Journal of Semitic Studies 16.2 (1971): 151–156.

works.title: A Grammar of Biblical Aramaic
works.what: A standard grammar of the parts of the Old Testament written in Aramaic, in Daniel and Ezra, with a verse of Jeremiah and two words of Genesis.
works.citation: Franz Rosenthal, A Grammar of Biblical Aramaic, Porta Linguarum Orientalium, n.s. 5 (Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz, 1961).
cites: Franz Rosenthal, A Grammar of Biblical Aramaic

works.plain: Book on the words of Jesus, 1902
works.title: The Words of Jesus
works.by: Gustaf Dalman; translated by D. M. Kay
works.what: A German scholar of Aramaic studies Jesus' sayings in the light of later Jewish writings and the Aramaic language.
works.citation: Gustaf Dalman, The Words of Jesus Considered in the Light of Post-Biblical Jewish Writings and the Aramaic Language, English translation by D. M. Kay (Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark, 1902).
cites: Gustaf Dalman, The Words of Jesus

works.title: Grammatik des jüdisch-palästinischen Aramäisch
works.what: A grammar, in German, of the Aramaic of Jewish writings from the land of Israel, such as the Jerusalem Talmud and the Targums.
works.citation: Gustaf Dalman, Grammatik des jüdisch-palästinischen Aramäisch nach den Idiomen des palästinischen Talmud und Midrasch, des Onkelostargum (Cod. Socini 84) und der jerusalemischen Targume zum Pentateuch, 2nd ed. (Leipzig: Hinrichs, 1905).
